cards.explanation: The answer is False. Peter says he'll always remind them "…even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have." (2 Peter 1:12) So the reminder isn't because they're shaky. A good reminder isn't an insult, friends, it's a hand on the shoulder. I've been reminded to preheat the oven for years and I still say thank you.

The answer is that the tent will be laid aside. Peter says he knows "…this tent will soon be laid aside…" (2 Peter 1:14) A tent is something you set down, not something you live in forever. And he still spends the time he has left looking after these believers, which tells me a lot about him.

The answer is our Lord Jesus Christ. Peter says it was "…as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me." (2 Peter 1:14) So this didn't come from a rumor or a hunch, friends. It came straight from the Lord he served.

The answer is "recall." Peter will make every effort so that after his departure they "…will be able to recall these things at all times." (2 Peter 1:15) He's thinking past his own lifetime. He wants these things to stay with them long after he's gone, and I think that's real love.

The answer is True. Peter says, "…we were eyewitnesses of His majesty." (2 Peter 1:16) They didn't hear it secondhand, friends, they were there. That's a whole different level than "I read it somewhere."

The answer is "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." (2 Peter 1:17) Think about who is speaking, bakers: God the Father, from the Majestic Glory. It's a Father saying it about His Son, and Peter says "…we ourselves heard this voice from heaven…" (2 Peter 1:18).

The answer is True. Peter says, "…we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain." (2 Peter 1:18) Notice the "ourselves," friends. They weren't told about it, they heard it.

The answer is False. Peter says the word of the prophets is "…confirmed beyond doubt." and "…you will do well to pay attention to it…" (2 Peter 1:19) So it's not something to set aside, friends. It's something to keep close, even after what they saw on the mountain.

The answer is a lamp shining in a dark place. Peter says to pay attention to it "…as to a lamp shining in a dark place…" (2 Peter 1:19) A lamp doesn't need to be fancy to matter, bakers. In the dark, it's the most important thing in the room.

The answer is until the day dawns and the morning star rises in their hearts. Peter says to pay attention to it "…until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts." (2 Peter 1:19) So the lamp is for the dark stretch, and Peter points ahead to the dawn. I won't guess more than the verse says, friends, but I do love a sunrise after a long night.

The answer is one's own interpretation. Peter says, "…no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation." (2 Peter 1:20) He calls it something to understand "above all," so he wants it to land, friends. Prophecy isn't something a person cooks up on their own.

The answer is True. Peter says, "…no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man…" (2 Peter 1:21) People didn't decide to start prophesying like picking a hobby, bakers. That leads right into what he says next about who carried them.
